label: input token h in the original phase
explanation: Fires on every step where the letter h is input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. Precision is 1.0 and recall is about 0.996. Magnitude falls with position: h at t=0 is maximal (all t=0 activations are in the top quartile), and h at t>=5 is almost entirely in the bottom quartile. Repeat occurrences of h tend to be somewhat weaker than the first. It never fires on the delimiter or on any other token. The only copy-phase activations are tiny (<0.1 of max) at recall_idx 1, when h is fed back as the first copied token in short sequences that start with h, and they carry about 0% of the mass.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.996, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9998, and there are 0 false positives.

The 403 test misses are all copy-phase steps where h is fed back at recall_idx 1, with activation 0.01-0.08 of max and about 0% of the mass. Restricting to (phase==2)&(in_tok==h)&(recall_idx==1)&(L==3) gives precision 0.92 and covers 407 steps, so 'short sequences' in fact means mostly L=3. This is negligible and is already disclosed in the explanation.

Magnitude claims hold. The h-at-t=0 predicate covers 61% of the top quartile with 16472 steps, about the size of a whole quartile, so all t=0 activations sit in the top quartile. h at t>=5 covers 97% of the bottom quartile and 5% of Q2, which matches 'almost entirely bottom quartile'. Repeat h at t>=3 (in_first==0) sits in Q1/Q2 with 0.6% in Q3 and 0% in Q4. First occurrences at t>=3 reach Q3 at 21%, so 'repeats weaker' holds.
The delimiter claim holds: 0 activations at phase 1, and the profile shows no activations on any in_tok other than h.
Minor wording issue: the label says 'original phase', but there are tiny copy-phase activations. They are disclosed, so the label does not meaningfully overclaim.
